headings.title: SMTO-RST-0019 — SMTO blocked an unsafe internal access to its saved data

html:
SMTO-RST-0019 — SMTO blocked an unsafe internal access to its saved data

GUID: c600850b-d983-5819-86c4-0aaa634df984
Slug: controller-sql-access-forbidden
Domain: RST · Subsystem: controller

What happened

  • Part of SMTO tried to read or write its saved data files directly while running, which isn't allowed, so SMTO stopped that step. This is a problem inside SMTO, not something you did.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Copy error details in this panel. The details record which part of SMTO tried the blocked access, which is what needs fixing.
  2. Look at the task or screen you were using to see whether your last action finished before you try it again. SMTO stopped the blocked step, so that action may not have completed.
  3. Don't open or change SMTO's data files with other programs while SMTO is running. SMTO only allows changes to those files through its own controlled steps, to keep your saved data intact.

What success looks like

  • The same action completes without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied details, and what you were doing when it appeared, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to repair or delete the data files yourself; repairs are done only while SMTO is stopped.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A runtime component opened or used a Controller- or Gateway-owned SQLite database outside its bootstrap, checkpoint or repair phase, and the SQLite access guard rejected it.

What this means

  • A Controller SQLite guard or Gateway recovery connection observes SQL access outside its authorized bootstrap/checkpoint/repair phase. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • A Controller SQLite guard or Gateway recovery connection observes SQL access outside its authorized bootstrap/checkpoint/repair phase.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the caller and lifecycle phase rather than relaxing the storage boundary.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the SQLiteAccessDenied reason and caller (sqlite_guard denial diagnostics, or GATEWAY_SQL_AUDIT_FILE records for the Gateway) and change that code path to use the in-memory repository API during normal operation. Perform storage repair only with the Server stopped, through the supported recovery owner in its BOOTSTRAP, CHECKPOINT or REPAIR phase.
  • Use the Controller repository API during normal operation. Perform storage repair only with the Server stopped and the supported recovery owner.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • Normal operations use the owning in-memory repository and permitted persistence uses its supported lifecycle.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
